name: Social Studies of Data Science & Engineering
description:
"Data is the new oil." This promise fuels the imagination of entrepreneurs, politicians, scientists, and developers alike. Indeed, data driven applications are increasingly becoming part of the fabric of contemporary life. Consequently, they give rise to  questions concerning their implications on various levels: Does Big Data constitue a new mode of knowledge production? What socio-technical challenges are concomitant with the deep integration of data mining, machine learning, and predictive analytics? 
The target audience of this course are scientists and practitioners involved in the development and implementation of Big Data applications. Starting from practical examples, students will be informed on and involved in current debates and controversies on Big Data. Issues to be considered include 'datafication' as theory driven practice, filter bubbles created by recommender systems or search engines and their effects on democracy, discrimination through algorithms, and the role of privacy and security in these developments.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of data science, good knowledge of English
